formerNames: North Okanagan/Columbia Shuswap Regional Health Board
organization.description: Regional health board under the Health Authorities Act, designated as the North Okanagan Regional Health Board on 28 November 1994. M444/1996 continued it in the December 1996 reconstitution. Those orders provided for 4 community health councils to amalgamate into it. Renamed by express amending orders, each dated by the day it was made. Amalgamated into the Interior Health Authority on 12 December 2001 under the Regional Health Boards Regulation, B.C. Reg. 293/2001, which names it in Schedule A (signed 11 December, deposited 12 December).

properties.name: Simon Fraser

properties.note: New Westminster is too small to resolve on the 1997/98 inset. The 2001 boundary schedule for this region names Burnaby and New Westminster, and the Statistics Canada map places New Westminster in Simon Fraser.

organization.officialName: East Kootenay Community Health Services Society
organization.description: Community health services society, registered on 13 March 1997 (S0036594), serving the areas of several community health councils where no regional board was formed. On 12 December 2001 its governors were replaced by the new authority's appointees (M298-M305/2001) and its services passed to the Interior Health Authority. The corporate registry records its dissolution on 15 February 2002. It is not in Schedule A of B.C. Reg. 293/2001, so this is a passing of services, not an amalgamation; how and when its assets were conveyed is not found.

Community health services society, registered on 13 March 1997 (S0036598), serving the areas of several community health councils where no regional board was formed. On 12 December 2001 its governors were replaced by the new authority's appointees (M298-M305/2001) and its services passed to the Interior Health Authority and the Northern Health Authority. Its territory was split: the Quesnel council went to Northern Health, the others to Interior Health; Bella Coola moved on to Vancouver Coastal in March 2002. The corporate registry records its dissolution on 15 February 2002. It is not in Schedule A of B.C. Reg. 293/2001, so this is a passing of services, not an amalgamation; how and when its assets were conveyed is not found.

One of five geographic health authorities created on 12 December 2001 by the Regional Health Boards Regulation (B.C. Reg. 293/2001). Schedule A amalgamates three regional boards into it: the Fraser Valley, Simon Fraser and South Fraser health regions.

One of five geographic health authorities created on 12 December 2001 by the Regional Health Boards Regulation (B.C. Reg. 293/2001). Schedule A amalgamates seventeen bodies into it: the Thompson, North Okanagan and Okanagan Similkameen health regions and fourteen councils and transitional authorities of the Kootenays and Cariboo. The East Kootenay, Kootenay Boundary and most of the Cariboo community health services societies’ services passed to it at the same time.

One of five geographic health authorities created on 12 December 2001 by the Regional Health Boards Regulation (B.C. Reg. 293/2001). Schedule A amalgamates thirteen bodies into it: the Northern Interior Regional Health Board and twelve northwest, northeast and Quesnel councils. The North West and Peace Liard societies’ services, and the Cariboo society’s in Quesnel, passed to it at the same time.

One of five geographic health authorities created on 12 December 2001 by the Regional Health Boards Regulation (B.C. Reg. 293/2001). Schedule A amalgamates five bodies into it: the Vancouver/Richmond Health Board, the North Shore Health Region and the Powell River, Sea to Sky and Sunshine Coast councils; the Coast Garibaldi society’s services passed to it. The Bella Coola and Central Coast areas joined it from Interior and Vancouver Island on 18 March 2002.

One of five geographic health authorities created on 12 December 2001 by the Regional Health Boards Regulation (B.C. Reg. 293/2001). Schedule A amalgamates six bodies into it: the Capital and Central Vancouver Island health regions and four councils and transitional authorities of the north island and Central Coast; the Upper Island/Central Coast society’s services passed to it. The Central Coast area moved to Vancouver Coastal on 18 March 2002.
